description: Replace the exact n=256 two-CTA epoch/polling path with graph-captured split-phase panel factor, solve, and triangular update kernels across the matrix batch. Right-size each stage to live work, reuse stable shape buffers, and overlap independent matrices to remove atomic polling and full-CTA fences while preserving every other dispatch, caller-stream semantics, caches, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Replaced exact batch64/n256 two-CTA epoch polling with a CUDA-graph-replayed right-looking schedule: one factor CTA per matrix, exact 192/128/64 solve grids, exact 384/192/64 triangular update grids, stage-specific 17.41/34.82/37.89 KiB shared workspaces, stable identity-cached buffers, and captured upper-copy preparation. The batch60/n1024 two-CTA factor remained isolated. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target n256 improved from the retained ~120.6 us to 116.406 us (112.642 best); aggregate measured 790.952 us versus parent 788.920 amid untouched-cell drift. Mandatory hosted index3 profile job c3e0eb64e3c04ac6a3ad04a9c6ddd9c8 ran 2026-07-20T03:16:02Z--03:22:31Z on this exact commit; canonical artifacts show factor/solve/update at 24.61/25.79/21.12 us, grids 64/192/384, 80/168/69 registers, 6.11/8.07/15.59% occupancy, and 82.72/76.32/64.00% no-eligible cycles.

Used the exact Trial0 profile's 64-block factor underfill by making triangular-update task0 factor the next diagonal in-place while the other 5/2/0 update tasks remain live, removing three separate factor graph nodes and preserving exact 384/192/64 update grids plus every external dispatch. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. The n256 distribution contained one 5.688 ms outlier: mean 128.595 us versus Trial0 116.406, but best improved sharply from 112.642 to 99.202 us. Aggregate measured 818.452 us versus 790.952, dominated by the n256 outlier and an unrelated n2048 99.9 ms outlier (2436.477 mean, 1911.296 best).

Removed the profiled 10.75-us generic grouped upper-copy graph node. Stable source/output Numba views now let stage0 factor, solve, and triangular-update kernels read each original input tile directly; those waves overwrite every physical-upper output tile, while the once-zeroed physical lower half remains untouched across replay. Later graph stages and all other dispatches remain unchanged. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial0 116.406 us and fused Trial1's 99.202-us best to 101.689 us mean (96.382 best), despite one 1.125-ms outlier. Aggregate reached 786.229 us, below the 788.920 parent and 790.952 Trial0.

Split each 64-column graph solve into two independent 32-column MathDx CTAs, doubling exact solve grids from 192/128/64 to 384/256/128 and reducing solve shared memory from 34.82 to 26.62 KiB. Slice build and wrapped Modal validation passed all 17 tests plus fresh-input guards. The slice-wrapped full benchmark then emitted no test or cell output for 736 seconds, exceeding task.yml's 600-second benchmark budget, and was terminated; the new half-panel device specialization did not produce an active-set metric.

Restored the successful full-width graph solver after Trial3's timeout, then changed only triangular-update scheduling from sample-major groups to task-major interleaving across all 64 matrices. Each factor-bearing diagonal update wave now launches across independent matrices before the remaining triangular tasks, while exact 384/192/64 grids, graph dependencies, direct stage0 reads, stable buffers, and all other dispatches stay fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 measured 101.376 us (95.084 best) versus Trial2 101.689/96.382; aggregate reached a branch-best 783.253 us versus Trial2 786.229 and parent 788.920.

Applied task-major interleaving to the 192/128/64 graph solve grids, removing general division/modulo from each CTA and launching identical panel workers across all 64 independent matrices before advancing the panel id. Update interleaving, fused next factors, direct stage0 reads, stable graph buffers, and every other dispatch stayed fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 mean was outlier-inflated to 103.326 us by one 2.270-ms sample, while its clean floor improved from Trial4 95.084 to 92.282 us; aggregate 803.215 was also dominated by an unrelated 100.8-ms n2048 outlier. Mandatory cadence profile job 135afa04f5364b88af1cc54a83e6e5a7 ran 2026-07-20T04:07:09Z--04:15:35Z on this exact commit. Canonical artifacts show factor 20.42 us/79 regs, solve waves 25.34/23.07/22.88 us at 96 regs, and fused update-factor waves 32.16/29.95/30.18 us at 80 regs, with no spills.

Acted on Trial5's ~30-us fused update/factor waves by recognizing triangular diagonal tasks as U^T U: each now loads one solved half tile and reuses it as both MathDx GEMM operands instead of loading the same global tile twice. Off-diagonal tasks retain paired operands; graph grids, matrix interleaving, stable buffers, direct stage0 reads, and all other paths stay fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved decisively from Trial5 103.326 mean/92.282 best and Trial4 101.376/95.084 to 91.117 us mean (87.286 best), versus the retained parent near 120.6 us. Aggregate measured 796.894, dominated by an unrelated 136.0-ms n2048 outlier and slower untouched n4096/large cells.

Specialized the final all-diagonal update/factor graph node: fixed stage2/stage3 coordinates, one U[2,3] half operand reused for U^T U, no generic task decoding/branch, and 27.65 KiB dynamic shared instead of 37.89 KiB. Earlier interleaved solve/update waves, direct source reads, stable graph buffers, and every external dispatch remain unchanged. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial6 91.117 us mean/87.286 best and Trial5's 92.282 best to 90.012 us mean (84.990 best), versus the retained parent near 120.6 us. Aggregate reached a new branch/global low of 780.307 us versus 783.253 Trial4 and 788.920 parent.

Specialized the 192-block middle update/factor graph node with fixed stage1 coordinates, task-major matrix mapping, direct diagonal/off-diagonal operand selection, no source branch, and no triangular decode loop; only task0 factorizes the known next diagonal. Stage0 generic and the specialized final wave remain unchanged. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 mean was inflated to 92.750 us by one 1.963-ms sample versus Trial7 90.012, while the clean floor improved from 84.990 to 82.880 us. Aggregate measured 784.805 us versus Trial7 780.307 amid slower n512/n1024/n2048 cells.

Completed stage specialization by replacing the 384-block initial update's dynamic triangular decoder and tile/source branches with fixed six-task mapping, direct original-source accumulators, known row0 operands, and task0-only factorization. Middle/final specialized nodes, solve/update interleaving, stable graphs, and all external dispatches stayed fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 mean was inflated to 94.421 us by one 2.374-ms sample; the clean floor was 82.676 us versus Trial8 82.880 and Trial7 84.990. Aggregate measured 788.827 us amid broad untouched-cell slowdown, including n4096 batch2 at 1703.223 us.

Fused the final 64-block solve and update/factor graph nodes: the solved FP32 U[2,3] panel is stored, converted directly to half in shared memory, factor storage is aliased for that half panel, panel storage is reused for the final accumulator, and one graph node/global panel reload is removed. Slice build passed, but the slice-wrapped Modal validation emitted no test output for 398 seconds (over four times the recorded 90-second allowance and beyond prior 375-second termination precedent) and was terminated. No active-set benchmark metric was produced; the exact source remains queued for an infrastructure retry after this required failure row.

Retried the exact fused final solve/update source after Trial10's pre-test infrastructure stall. Slice-wrapped validation then completed normally with all 17 tests and fresh-input guards passing, and the full 15-cell benchmark passed. The single final 64-block node solves U[2,3], converts it FP32-to-half in aliased shared storage, updates/factors tile3,3, and removes one graph node plus a global panel reload. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial7 90.012 us mean/84.990 best and Trial9's 82.676 best to 86.420 us mean (82.560 best), despite one 824-us outlier. Aggregate reached a new branch/global low of 778.836 us versus 780.307 Trial7 and 788.920 parent.

Replaced the remaining runtime-parameterized solve operator with independent initial and middle graph kernels: fixed source/output selection, diagonal/panel coordinates, and exact 192/128-block grids remove scalar arguments, branches, and tile arithmetic while preserving task-major matrix interleaving. The fused final solve/update and all specialized updates remain fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from the fused Trial11 86.420 us mean/82.560 best and Trial9's 82.676 floor to 83.180 us mean (79.072 best), versus the retained parent near 120.6 us. Aggregate reached a new branch/global low of 773.681 us versus 778.836 Trial11 and 788.920 parent. Per manager coordination, no new hosted request was launched.

Replaced scalar FP32 graph-stage entry loads with 16-byte cp.async tile transfers: initial factor uses one full-tile group, while initial/middle solve and the fused final solve use paired factor/panel groups from their exact source arrays, eliminating redundant load loops and barriers without changing update operands or graph topology. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial12 83.180 us mean/79.072 best to 76.470 us mean/70.910 best; aggregate improved from 773.681 to 771.154 us. No hosted profile was launched pending the manager-owned run-wide slot.

Extended Trial13 16-byte cp.async FP32 transfers to the six initial-update accumulators, three middle-update accumulators, and fused-final tile3,3 accumulator; FP32-to-FP16 operand loads and graph topology remain unchanged. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial13 76.470 us mean/70.910 best to 74.917 us mean/70.912 best; aggregate improved from 771.154 to 768.640 us. The single run-wide hosted profile of exact Trial13 commit 2f94e5f, index3, job fe549f03612c4c688a0466986b1e6e41 ran 2026-07-20T05:15:15Z--05:30:38Z; canonical artifacts show factor 17.41 us, initial/middle solve 20.96/16.06 us, initial/middle update 25.95/22.05 us, and fused final 44.06 us with 86.45 percent no-eligible cycles.

Replaced scalar Numba FP32-to-FP16 update-operand staging with C device helpers that issue aligned 16-byte float4 global loads and packed half2 shared stores for both reused diagonal tiles and off-diagonal tile pairs. Async FP32 accumulators, graph nodes, and MathDx operators remain fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 moved from Trial14 74.917 us mean/70.912 best to 74.876 us mean/70.912 best. Aggregate measured 770.742 us versus Trial14 768.640, with slower untouched large cells accounting for the aggregate drift.

Replaced the fused-final kernel scalar shared FP32-to-FP16 panel conversion with aligned float4 shared loads and packed half2 stores before its last diagonal update/factor. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 mean was outlier-inflated from Trial15 74.876 to 80.846 us by one 2.095 ms sample, while the clean floor improved from 70.912 to 70.400 us. Aggregate measured 780.493 us amid broad untouched-cell slowdown, including batch640/n512 1022.268 us and batch8/n2048 1937.736 us.

Added a stable graph-captured FP16 tile sidecar: initial/middle solve kernels dual-store solved FP32 panels plus packed half tiles, and update kernels cp.async the half sidecar instead of reloading/converting FP32 output. Slice build and all 17 validation tests plus fresh-input guards passed because those tests do not enter the exact batch64/n256 dispatch. The full benchmark passed cells0-2, then JIT specialization at cell3 rejected the sidecar argument as float32* against the declared float16* device helper; the sidecar used the default Numba array view instead of the existing half view, so no active-set metric was produced.

Fixed Trial17 by exposing the stable sidecar through the existing FP16 Numba CUDA-array view. Initial/middle solves now dual-store each solved panel to FP32 output and packed FP16 sidecar; the following update waves use 16-byte cp.async half tile/pair loads from that sidecar. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 mean was inflated to 92.189 us by one 4.400 ms sample, while the floor improved from Trial16 70.400 to 70.382 us. Aggregate measured 786.352 us amid broad untouched-cell slowdown.

Repeated the exact corrected FP16 sidecar source after Trial18 single-sample inflation. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed again. Batch64/n256 produced a second improved clean floor of 70.348 us versus Trial18 70.382 and pre-sidecar Trial16 70.400, but another isolated 3.530 ms sample inflated its mean to 87.779 us. Aggregate measured 783.021 us amid slower untouched high-batch cells. The repeated floor preserves evidence for the dual-store plus direct-half cp.async structure while mean impact remains masked by hosted outliers.

Packed graph FP16 sidecar tiles from global LD80 to LD64 while retaining LD80 MathDx shared destinations. Each solved panel now occupies contiguous 128-byte rows; dual stores write packed rows and update cp.async helpers transfer them into padded shared rows. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 clean floor improved from Trial19 70.348 to 70.322 us, but one 2.227 ms sample inflated mean to 81.213 us. Aggregate measured 778.368 us amid slower untouched high-batch cells.

Compacted the packed LD64 graph sidecar from a sparse 16-tile matrix layout to the five solved panels actually consumed: row0 columns1-3 and row1 columns2-3. This cuts the batch sidecar from 8 MiB to 2.5 MiB without changing solve dual-stores or update cp.async transfers. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 returned to 75.209 us mean despite one 1.027 ms sample, and its clean floor improved from Trial20 70.322 to 70.274 us. Aggregate measured 774.653 us.

Co-issued each update CTA FP32 accumulator cp.async group with its single or paired FP16 sidecar operand group, then used one wait_group and one CTA barrier before MathDx instead of serial load/wait/barrier phases. The compact five-tile LD64 sidecar and solve dual-stores remain fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial21 75.209 us mean/70.274 best to 73.385 us mean/70.142 best despite one 0.671 ms sample. Aggregate reached 769.570 us, near Trial14 branch-best 768.640 amid slower untouched large cells.

Changed every D256 MathDx FP16 shared operand leading dimension from 80 to 64, aligning shared tiles with packed sidecar rows and reducing update dynamic shared memory from 37.89 to 33.00 KiB while retaining co-issued transfers. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 regressed from Trial22 73.385 us mean/70.142 best to 84.824 us mean/74.880 best, with one 1.992 ms sample; the clean-floor regression shows the power-of-two shared layout cost outweighed residency. Aggregate measured 783.633 us.

Changed the power-of-two LD64 FP16 shared operands to LD72 while retaining packed LD64 sidecar rows and co-issued FP32/FP16 transfers. This preserves non-power-of-two bank spacing and keeps update dynamic shared memory below the original LD80 layout. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 recovered from Trial23 84.824 us mean/74.880 best to 74.077 us mean/70.140 best despite one 0.814 ms sample. Aggregate reached a new branch low of 768.091 us versus Trial14 768.640.

Replaced scalar Numba output drains with aligned float4 C device stores for full tiles and a specialized float4-plus-boundary masked path for upper-triangular diagonal tiles. This covers factor, update, and fused-final stores; solve dual-stores were already vectorized. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 clean floor improved materially from Trial24 70.140 to 69.440 us, while one 1.088 ms sample inflated mean to 75.114 us. Aggregate measured 776.255 us amid slower untouched n512/n2048/n4096 cells.

Fused the final solved-panel FP32 output store with its shared FP16 conversion in one float4/half2 C device pass. The 64-block final node now reads the solved panel once and removes one CTA barrier before loading its final diagonal accumulator; vectorized stores, LD72 shared operands, compact sidecar, and co-issued update loads remain fixed. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial25 75.114 us mean/69.440 best to 73.525 us mean/69.116 best despite one 0.877 ms sample. Aggregate reached a new branch low of 767.908 us.

Extended the fused final solved-panel drain so each thread stores its float4 output and half2 shared operand, then immediately cp.async-prefetches the matching final-diagonal accumulator segment back into the now-dead panel address. One wait/barrier replaces the separate conversion barrier plus accumulator load phase. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved from Trial26 73.525 us mean/69.116 best to 71.560 us mean/68.480 best despite one 0.606 ms sample. Aggregate reached a new branch low of 765.844 us versus 767.908.

Removed the underfilled 64-block initial factor graph node. Each of the three 192-block initial-solve workers per matrix now loads/factorizes tile0,0 locally before TRSM, and worker0 vector-stores the returned diagonal; duplicated factor work trades for greater parallel exposure and one fewer node/dependency. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 measured 72.023 us mean/68.712 best versus Trial27 71.560/68.480, with one 0.712 ms sample. Aggregate reached a new branch low of 765.033 us versus 765.844.

Reduced the middle update node from three tasks to two diagonal-only CTAs per matrix with a one-operand 26 KiB workspace, then folded the U12-transpose-U13 off-diagonal update into the existing final solve/update/factor CTA before loading factor2,2 and solving U23. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 clean floor regressed from Trial28 68.712 to 69.634 us; one 1.299 ms sample inflated mean to 76.255 us. Aggregate measured 769.712 us versus 765.033, exposing the new final node serial factor-load phase.

Expanded the fused final node's shared workspace and co-issued the factor(2,2) cp.async load with the off-diagonal accumulator and paired FP16 sidecar operands, removing the serial post-GEMM factor-load phase exposed by Trial29. Wrapped build, all 17 official tests, and the batch8/n256 fresh-input guard passed. The full active benchmark rejected exact batch64/n256 because output contained NaN or Inf: the eager factor read can race the concurrently produced middle diagonal at full batch, so no complete aggregate metric was emitted.

Acted on the exact final hosted profile by giving the 192-block initial factor/solve node dedicated 256-thread MathDx POTRF/TRSM operators while confining vector loads/stores to the proven first 128 lanes. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, and fresh-input guard passed, but the locked benchmark produced NaN/Inf at batch64/n256 (and subsequently batch60/n1024), so no complete metric was emitted. The motivating exact ca5edb0 index3 profile launched 2026-07-20T10:34:03Z and succeeded as job 2c0c618e71284675b77e327f0871a379: initial/final nodes measured 43.01/41.54 us with 8.16/6.34% occupancy and 82.67/85.84% no-eligible cycles. Canonical report, details, and zip are under autocuda/profiles/2026-07-19-01-44-06-cholesky-resumed-local-unmerged/brief-71-trial-28-ca5edb0ed732d4a83bd30280b1c8c6993bef7818.*. No second hosted request was launched.

Acted on the exact ca5edb0 profile's serial 192/384/128/192/64-node underfill by partitioning the 64 matrices 16/48 across two disjoint graph branches, switching stage launch maps to (sample,task), and joining both caller-ordered queues before return. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, and fresh-input guard passed. The full wrapped benchmark emitted no cell output for 677.636 seconds, beyond the recorded 600-second task budget, and was terminated; multi-queue capture/replay did not produce an active-set metric. No additional hosted profile was launched.

Narrowed the profile-guided initial-node width experiment to dedicated 192-thread MathDx POTRF/TRSM operators, retaining the proven 128-lane vector load/store mapping while exposing six warps per each of 192 CTAs instead of four. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 regressed from parent Trial28 72.023 us mean/68.712 best to 181.412/169.472 us, and aggregate measured 836.291 us; the extra MathDx participation cost outweighed increased warp exposure. No additional hosted profile was launched.

Returned to the separate-factor Trial27 lineage and widened only its underfilled 64-block initial factor node to a dedicated 256-thread MathDx POTRF, while keeping every solve/update/final node at the proven 128-thread widths and limiting vector I/O to the original 128 lanes. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 regressed from Trial27 71.560 us mean/68.480 best to 74.253/70.018 us; aggregate measured 771.603 us. The extra factor warps did not offset wider MathDx cost. No new hosted request was launched.

Completed the standalone initial-factor width sweep at 192 threads, preserving Trial34's dedicated factor operator and original 128-lane cp.async/store mapping while every solve/update node remained unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 improved over the 256-thread Trial34 from 74.253/70.018 us to 73.356/69.758 us, but remained above the 128-thread Trial27 at 71.560/68.480 us. Aggregate measured 767.976 us. No hosted profile was launched.

Completed the standalone initial-factor width sweep at 160 threads, using five MathDx warps while preserving the 128-lane vector I/O and all downstream 128-thread graph nodes. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch64/n256 measured 73.779 us mean/69.884 best versus 192-thread Trial35 73.356/69.758, 256-thread Trial34 74.253/70.018, and the retained 128-thread Trial27 71.560/68.480. Aggregate measured 769.319 us. No hosted request was launched.

Selected clean exact commit ca5edb0ed732d4a83bd30280b1c8c6993bef7818 after 37 logged trials. It replaces epoch polling with graph-replayed factor/solve/update stages, direct cp.async FP32/FP16 staging, a compact five-tile sidecar, LD68/LD72 operands, vectorized/fused stores, and initial-factor duplication across 192 solve CTAs; all required checks passed at 765.033 us aggregate and batch64/n256 72.023 us mean/68.712 best. Trial27 1d28e315 remains the lower target floor at 71.560/68.480 us and 765.844 aggregate. The single authorized exact final profile launched 2026-07-20T10:34:03Z on ca5edb0 index3, succeeded at 10:48:28Z as job 2c0c618e71284675b77e327f0871a379, and no second request launched; canonical report/details/zip are profiles/2026-07-19-01-44-06-cholesky-resumed-local-unmerged/brief-71-trial-28-ca5edb0ed732d4a83bd30280b1c8c6993bef7818.*. It measured initial solve 43.01 us (119 regs, 34.82 KiB, 8.16% occupancy, 82.67% no-eligible), update 22.98 us, middle solve/update 16.70/21.47 us, and final fused node 41.54 us (96 regs, 34.82 KiB, 6.34% occupancy, 85.84% no-eligible). Post-profile Trial30's eager factor prefetch raced its producer; Trial31's 256-thread initial role produced NaN/Inf; Trial32's 16/48 two-queue graph hung; Trial33's 192-thread initial role regressed target to 181.412 us; and separate-factor 160/192/256-thread Trials34-36 measured 73.779/73.356/74.253 us target versus Trial27's 71.560, preserving 128 threads as the measured width. Keep this line moving with source-level initial/final register-lifetime reduction at 128 threads, a dependency-correct 32-column final solve that raises the 64-block node's useful grid, a single-capture event-joined matrix pipeline, or MathDx-compatible update operand swizzles addressing the profile's 2.0x shared-load and 3.1x shared-store conflicts.
